Question B-005-009-007.

Why the correct answer is right: A polarized electrolytic capacitor has a required voltage polarity. Reverse voltage can damage its insulating layer and make the part fail.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Do not parallel with capacitors other than electrolytics": The safety issue is polarity; mixing capacitor types in parallel can be valid when voltage ratings and circuit needs are suitable.
- sourceIndex 2: "Use them exclusively at radio frequencies": Electrolytics are commonly used for power-supply filtering and other low-frequency or direct-current (DC) related jobs, not exclusively at radio frequencies.
- sourceIndex 3: "Do not use them in series combinations": Series use is not the central precaution. Each electrolytic still needs protection from reverse voltage and excessive stress.
